# University of Chicago – Summary
The University of Chicago is a prestigious private research university located in Chicago's Hyde Park and Woodlawn neighborhoods, spanning a 217-acre campus renowned for its Gothic and modern architectural styles. Founded in 1890, the university pioneered the liberal arts undergraduate core curriculum and the Socratic method, and is organized into the College (with 51 majors and 33 minors), four graduate divisions (biological sciences, humanities, physical sciences, social sciences), and seven professional schools—including the top-ranked Booth School of Business and Law School. The university operates on a quarter system, supports extensive interdisciplinary research through more than 140 research centers, and manages major national labs such as Argonne and Fermi. The university maintains a global presence with affiliated centers in Hong Kong, London, Paris, Beijing, New Delhi, and a marine biological laboratory in Woods Hole, Massachusetts.
Admissions to the University of Chicago are highly competitive, with a dramatic drop in undergraduate acceptance rates from 71% in 1996 to 4.7% in 2023. The current student body (as of fall 2024) comprises over 7,500 undergraduates and 10,900 graduate students, with 18% of undergraduates being international and a diverse racial makeup. The university is need-blind for domestic applicants. The University of Chicago boasts a distinguished roster of achievements, including 101 Nobel laureates, significant scientific discoveries (such as the first controlled nuclear chain reaction and the development of radiocarbon dating), and influential academic movements like the Chicago schools of economics and sociology. The university’s library system is extensive, containing over 11 million volumes, and its main athletic teams—the Chicago Maroons—compete in NCAA Division III. The University also fosters a vibrant student life, with more than 400 student organizations, a distinctive house-based residential system, and time-honored traditions such as the Scavenger Hunt and the Latke-Hamantash Debate.
